item.title: Sjta 2025 09 02
item.description:
विश्वास-टिप्पनी - HBV

Gajapati said one could do it any day within the 9-day duration. They still prefer to disobey it.

Sjta could’ve cited HBV 14.327 to make their case.
Otherwise, purANa verses can be interpreted to specifically apply to puri.

In Vilāsa 14, Verse 327 (numbered as 14.104 in some editions), Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī instructs that specific festivals of Lord Jagannātha must be celebrated in exact alignment with the dates and timings observed at the Mūla-pīṭha in Jagannātha Purī:

किन्त्वीदृग्भक्तिसन्दर्शि-जगन्नाथानुसारतः । दोलाचन्दन-कीलालरथयात्राइश्च कारयेत् ॥३२७॥

“Practices of bhakti, such as Dola Yātrā, Candana Yātrā, Snāna [Kīlāla] Yātrā, and Ratha Yātrā, should be performed in accordance with [the practices of] Lord Jagannātha [i.e., they should be performed on the same day that they are performed in Śrī Jagannātha Purī].”

Gaudiya Vaiṣṇava ācāryas have historically referenced this verse to settle disputes regarding astrological calculations (tithis). For instance, Śrīla Bhakti Sundar Govinda Dev-Gosvāmī Mahārāj explained:

“In the scriptures, there are so many procedures within vaidhi-bhakti. When there are complications in the laws for vaidhi-bhakti, Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī said that we should follow the dates observed by Lord Jagannāth… This means we will observe services to the Lord such as Ratha Yātrā and Chandan Yātrā on the day these services are being offered to Jagannāth.”

This verse establishes that the specific festive calendar of Jagannātha Purī acts as the universal standard for these celebrations elsewhere.
